A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CultureSteer research, with matching methods, datasets, and core experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Llama/Qwen word-association evaluations, steering ablations, WVS/BLEnD transfer results, and a language-control experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds cultural-model comparison results and an alternative-metric evaluation in Table 6.

M1.justification: CultureSteer's culture-specific linear transformation, one-hot control, residual steering, supervised training, and word-association inference remain unchanged. Equations 1–7 retain the same procedures and definitions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 881 SWOW cues, 22 semantic categories, English/Chinese data, and USA/UK/OC/CN cultural groups. WVS, BLEnD, and the Chinese-to-English control retain their existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands beyond vanilla models, CSP, and CCT to include CultureLLM and SimLLMCultureDist for both backbones, plus CultureMerge and CultureSPA for Llama. This substantially broadens comparisons to cultural adaptation methods. The downstream comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds evaluation of the main WAT comparison using a metric described as DCG, while retaining the original datasets and settings. v2 also specifies a LLaMA3.1-8B adaptation for the newly evaluated CultureLLM baseline. Existing splits, prompts, and training budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B and Table 6 examine whether conclusions persist under an alternative ranking metric. The steering-removal/mismatch experiments, language ablation, semantic-category analyses, and 'red' case study are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial numerical evidence for four cultural-model baselines, and Table 6 introduces alternative-metric results across models and cultures. Existing CultureSteer scores and Tables 2–3 remain unchanged. Llama CSP's average PWR@10 changes from 37.28 to 37.25.

T1.justification: Appendix B introduces a WAT-specific relevance definition based on each predicted word's human-association rank, together with the DCG formulation in Equations 8–9. Existing mathematical definitions and steering assumptions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: WAT-based cultural evaluation, CultureSteer mitigation, Western cultural bias, and downstream generalization. Rewording and additional comparisons do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly suggests overfitting or cultural knowledge interference as explanations for weaker fine-tuned comparators. Appendix B adds a claim that conclusions are robust to metric choice. The stated limitations and earlier analysis interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/resources repository link, a CultureMerge checkpoint link, and CultureLLM backbone-adaptation information. It removes the explicit LLaMAFactory implementation mention. Existing preprocessing instructions, prompt templates, hardware, and hyperparameter values are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds pre-LLM word-association studies and discussion of CultureBank, CultureLLM, and SimLLMCultureDist. The introduction adds diagnostic-task motivation from Zhou et al. (2025b). These additions refine positioning around earlier association models and cultural fine-tuning without replacing the research agenda.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, affiliations, abstract, introductory framing, related work, and baseline-description paragraphs. It adds acknowledgments and a metric appendix, shifting later appendix labels. Most methodological and analytical prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands and consolidates method labels into a shared column; a new metric-results table is added. Existing tables and figures are redistributed, and Figure 2 receives small graphical edits. The empirical plots retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The expanded cultural-model comparisons address v1's limited baseline coverage, and added access information improves auditability. However, the new metric validation mixes DCG/NDCG terminology and contains contradictory results: Table 6's Llama UK CultureSteer score falls from 1.94 at K=10 to 1.16 at K=20 despite the stated nonnegative cumulative formula. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are reporting or calculation errors, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
